hints: Notice the drop of mass $m$ is held stationary, so its downward weight $mg$ must be exactly balanced by an upward electric force.
Connect the voltage $V$ and plate separation $d$ to the uniform field strength using $E = V/d$, and the $n$ excess electrons to total charge $q = ne$.
Set $mg = qE = neV/d$ and rearrange to make $n$ the subject to compare with the four expressions.
walkthrough: Identify forces: stationary means resultant force is zero, so upward electric force $F$ equals downward weight $W = mg$.
State the field: for parallel plates with voltage $V$ and separation $d$, the uniform electric field strength is $E = V/d$.
State the charge: with $n$ excess electrons each of charge $e$, the drop charge magnitude is $q = ne$.
Set up force balance: $qE = mg$, so $(ne)(V/d) = mg$.
Rearrange for $n$: multiply both sides by $d$ and divide by $eV$ to get $n = mgd/eV$.

options.A: This is the reciprocal of the correct expression, giving $1/n$ rather than $n$.
options.B: Balancing weight $mg$ with electric force $neV/d$ gives $n = mgd/eV$.
options.C: This has $m$ in the numerator and $g$ in the denominator, so weight is not correctly represented as $mg$.
options.D: This omits $m$ from the weight and inverts $V$, so it does not satisfy $mg = neV/d$.
